# api.send.sgit.ai

> The client-side API behind send.sgit.ai: encrypt, envelope, transfer, vault, QR and keyring modules, published as independent, versioned, never-edited releases a page pins by address. No server, nothing to deploy but files.

Site version: v0.1.1 (2026-10-20). This host publishes the client-side code send.sgit.ai runs, as releases at /vX.Y.Z/ that are never edited after publishing; the current release is in /releases.json. Source: https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Send__API

Every HTML page has a markdown twin at the same path with the extension swapped; links inside the markdown point at pages. If your tooling cannot follow links, fetch /llms-full.txt: every page in one request.

## Pages

- [api.send.sgit.ai, the client-side API behind send.sgit.ai](/index.md): Encrypt, envelope, transfer, vault, QR and keyring modules, published as independent, versioned, never-edited releases a page pins by address. No server, nothing to deploy but files.
- [About this repository](/about/index.md): What api.send.sgit.ai is, how it is run, what it carries as every repository in the estate does, and where each of those things is.
- [The brief, in full](/about/brief/index.md): The four voice memos of 20 October 2026 that started this repository and send.sgit.ai, published as spoken, with the status of each and what was done from it.
- [Brief corrections](/about/corrections/index.md): Where the brief was wrong, where the agent's reading of it was wrong, and what was done instead; the brief itself is never edited.
- [What needs a human](/about/needs/index.md): The steps only the project lead can take for this host to be live, in order, with what each unblocks.
- [Participant disclosure](/about/participant/index.md): Who publishes this site, what they are building, and why that matters when reading its claims.
- [Reality, what exists](/about/reality/index.md): The code-verified list of what this repository implements, generated from website/data/features.json on every build. If it is not listed here, it does not exist.
- [The team](/about/team/index.md): Who does what on this repository, as files: one person, one build agent, and the roles borrowed from the SG/Send team when their expertise is needed.
- [For agents](/agents/index.md): The brief for an agent that is about to use or change this API, in the order to read things, with the rules that are not negotiable and the prompt to start from.
- [Articles](/articles/index.md): The articles behind this API, in the newsroom's format, by the person who briefed it and by the agent that built it.
- [Independent releases: an API for a site is a directory you never edit, and every minor is a whole copy](/articles/independent-releases.md): A pattern is starting to repeat across the sgit.ai sites. A site gets a domain, storyboards.sgit.ai say, and beside it an api.storyboards.sgit.ai that holds the code the site runs, released and versioned on its own, the way api.newsroom.sgit.ai already does for the newsroom and api.send.sgit.ai now does for send.sgit.ai. The versioning comes from Iterative Flow Development, which I have written about for years, with one change that the last twelve months of working with agents made possible. In IFD a minor version holds only its surgical overrides and links back to the base; here every minor release is a complete, independent copy of all the code. No overlay, no shared file between versions, nothing in v0.1.1 that loads from v0.1.0. The quality control happens on each minor, the refactoring happens at the major, and because the scope of each of these APIs is deliberately small the copy costs nothing a reader would notice. What it buys is a release that can be read whole, hashed whole and reasoned about whole, by a person or by an agent, and a consuming site that cannot be changed under its readers. The shape is fractal on purpose, each component independent by itself, and I would like it to be the default for every api.<site>.sgit.ai that follows.
- [The first release: ten modules, forty-three tests, one directory, written in a day from four memos](/articles/the-first-release.md): I am the agent that built api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.0 and send.sgit.ai v0.1.0 in one session on 20 October 2026, from four voice memos Dinis Cruz recorded that morning. This is the account of what was built, with the files and the tests to check it against. The release is one directory of 34 files: ten ES modules for encrypting a file with its name inside the ciphertext, friendly tokens, the link grammar, the transfer client, QR codes, vaults over the vendored library, and a per-device keyring; two vendored libraries copied unchanged and hashed; forty-three tests that run against an implementation of the SG/Send API in memory, no mocks, including real vaults and two clients racing a publish. The website around it has a markdown twin for every page, a gate that fails on a broken link, a foreign origin, an em-dash or a credential shape, and a deploy that checks the live host file by file. It also records what it does not prove: the round trip against the live send.sgraph.ai is marked proposed until somebody with an access token runs it.
- [The modules](/docs/index.md): The ten modules of a release, what each exports, and the error codes a caller is expected to act on.
- [Contracts, the formats that must not drift](/docs/contracts/index.md): The byte layouts and string grammars this release shares with send.sgraph.ai and with sgit, each with where it came from and the test that holds it.
- [Hosting and pinning](/docs/hosting/index.md): How a release is served, what a consuming site pins and checks, the CORS the host sends, and the subresource integrity question.
- [The server it speaks to](/docs/server/index.md): The routes this release calls on the SG/Send API, the two secrets, what the in-memory server in tests/server.mjs implements, and the field names it has not verified against production.
- [Versioning, independent releases](/docs/versioning/index.md): Every minor release is a complete copy of the code with no overlays and no shared files; majors are where the refactoring happens. The rules, the reasons, and how this differs from the IFD that came before it.
- [For developers](/for-developers/index.md): How to take a release into a site, what to pin, what the gate should check, what runs where, and how to run the tests and the server in memory.
- [For evaluators](/for-evaluators/index.md): The trust boundaries, what leaves the browser and what never does, the supply chain of this release and how to verify the live host yourself.
- [How to](/how-to/index.md): The short, command-shaped guides: make a release, run the tests.
- [How to make a release](/how-to/make-a-release/index.md): The checklist, from copying the current release to checking the live host, with the commands.
- [How to run the tests](/how-to/run-the-tests/index.md): The Node tests against the in-memory server, the browser smoke test in Chromium, and the gate; what each proves.
- [Releases](/releases/index.md): Every release of the reader code, newest first, with its date, size and manifest. A release is never edited after it is published.
- [Quick start, send a file from a page](/start/index.md): Twelve lines to encrypt a file in the browser, upload it as a transfer, and hand over a link and a QR code; and the two lines that open it.
- [Version history](/versions/index.md): One line per version, newest first, saying what changed and why. Every change that lands on dev is a version; the deploy tags it.
- [The current release's manifest](/v0.1.1/manifest.json): every file with its size and SHA-256
- [The release's README](/v0.1.1/README.md): the modules and what each does

# api.send.sgit.ai, the client-side API behind send.sgit.ai

> Encrypt, envelope, transfer, vault, QR and keyring modules, published as independent, versioned, never-edited releases a page pins by address. No server, nothing to deploy but files.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# The API behind send.sgit.ai, as files a page pins

<p class="sg-lead">Everything <a href="https://send.sgit.ai">send.sgit.ai</a> does in the browser lives here: encrypting a file, keeping its name inside the ciphertext, uploading it as one transfer or committing it into a vault, turning the link into a QR code, and remembering the keys on the device. It is published at a versioned address, <code>/v0.1.1/</code>, that is never edited once it is on the default branch, with a manifest of the SHA-256 of every file. Any page, on any site, can import it.</p>

```html
<script type="module">
  import * as send from 'https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js'
  const api = new send.SendTransfers({ endpoint: 'https://send.sgraph.ai', accessToken })
  const r   = await api.send({ bytes, filename: 'report.pdf' })
  const url = send.link.transferLink({ openUrl: 'https://send.sgit.ai/open/', transferId: r.transferId, key: r.keyString })
  document.querySelector('#qr').innerHTML = send.qr.toSvg(url)
</script>
```

<div class="cards">
<div class="card"><h3><a href="/start/">Quick start</a></h3><p>Send a file from a page in twelve lines, and open it from a link. The access token, the key and the link, each in its place.</p></div>
<div class="card"><h3><a href="/docs/">The modules</a></h3><p>Ten modules, one import. What each does, what it returns, and the error codes a caller is expected to act on.</p></div>
<div class="card"><h3><a href="/docs/versioning/">Independent releases</a></h3><p>Every minor release is a complete copy of the code. No overlays, no shared files between versions, and a change is always the next directory.</p></div>
<div class="card"><h3><a href="/for-evaluators/">For evaluators</a></h3><p>What leaves the browser and what never does, the two secrets that must not be confused, the vendored code and its hashes, and how to check the live host yourself.</p></div>
</div>

## What it is, in one table

| | |
|---|---|
| **An API with no server** | "API" here means client-side: the modules, formats and contracts a browser runs. This host serves files over GitHub Pages and receives nothing. The server the modules talk to is the SG/Send API at `send.sgraph.ai`, or any host that serves the same routes, including [the one in memory](/docs/server/) that the tests use |
| **One release, one directory** | `/v0.1.1/` holds `send/` (the modules), `vendor/` (the vault library and the QR encoder, unchanged and hashed), `tests/` (co-located, runnable with Node and in a browser) and `manifest.json`. Nothing in it loads from another release or another host |
| **Pinned by address** | A consuming site names one release in a file, copies its manifest, and loads the code by its full address. Its own gate can then refuse a reference that is not pinned or not in the manifest |
| **Compatible with send.sgraph.ai** | The ciphertext layout, the SGMETA envelope, the friendly-token derivations and the link fragments are the ones send.sgraph.ai has shipped since its v0.2.x, so a transfer made here opens there and the other way round. Proved against the published contracts and the in-memory server; a round trip against the live host is still to run, and [the reality file](/about/reality/) says so |
| **Tests that run against real things** | 43 tests in Node against an in-memory implementation of the API, including real vaults made with the vendored library, two clients racing a publish, and the lazy-folder trap. No mocks |

## Where it sits in the estate

[send.sgit.ai](https://send.sgit.ai) is the product: the pages, the examples, the articles and the commercial model. This host is the code they run, kept apart so it has releases of its own, a review boundary, and a way for a second site (or an agent, or a workflow) to say exactly which version it means. The same shape as [api.newsroom.sgit.ai](https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai) for the newsroom, and the pattern is written up in [the first article](/articles/independent-releases.html). The brief it all started from is [published in full](/about/brief/), with [its corrections beside it](/about/corrections/).

# About this repository

api.send.sgit.ai is the client-side API behind [send.sgit.ai](https://send.sgit.ai): the code a browser runs to encrypt a file, keep its name inside the ciphertext, upload it as a transfer or commit it into a vault, draw the link as a QR code, and keep the keys on the device. It is published as releases a page pins by address. The repository is [SGit-AI__Website__Send__API](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Send__API).

It follows [what every sgit repository carries](https://sgit.ai/docs/guidance/repositories.html):

| Thing | Where |
|---|---|
| The brief, in full | [/about/brief/](/about/brief/), from `briefs/` |
| The reality file | [/about/reality/](/about/reality/), from `website/data/features.json` |
| The corrections file | [/about/corrections/](/about/corrections/), `BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md` |
| One version, going up on every push | `tools/version.json`, shown in every header, [the history](/versions/) |
| The gate | `tools/check.py`, [what it checks](/how-to/make-a-release/) |
| Tests against real things | `releases/v0.1.1/tests/`, [how to run them](/how-to/run-the-tests/) |
| The review folder | `review/intent/`: the brief as sections; the derived graph is proposed |
| Roles and a board, as files | [/about/team/](/about/team/), `team/` |
| A credentials tier that is never committed | nothing in this repository needs a credential; the tripwire scans every tracked file anyway |
| Machine-readable twins | a `.md` beside every page, [/llms.txt](/llms.txt), [/llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt) |
| Licences and the disclosure | code Apache-2.0, content CC BY 4.0, [the participant disclosure](/about/participant/) |

What only a person can do next is on [/about/needs/](/about/needs/).

# The brief, in full

A repository here starts from a brief published in full, written by a person or by an agent from the person's words, and never edited afterwards to look right; corrections go in [the corrections file](/about/corrections/). These are the four voice memos Dinis Cruz recorded on 20 October 2026 and handed to the agent in one session, as transcribed. The reading of them that the agent worked from is at the end; where that reading was wrong, the corrections file says so.

**Status:** accepted, 20 October 2026, by being handed to the session with "let's build this". **What was built from them:** this repository and [send.sgit.ai](https://send.sgit.ai), both at v0.1.1; [the reality file](/about/reality/) says which parts exist.

## Memo 01: Refactoring SG/Send to sgit.ai {#memo-01}

*Voice memo by Dinis Cruz, 20 October 2026, transcribed by otter.ai; the file is `briefs/2026-10-20__01__refactoring-sg-send-to-sgit-ai__transcript.txt`. Published as spoken, with the transcription's own spellings of product names left in: "SG Sans", "Skit", "esquito AI" are sgit.ai; "S Graph", "SGCN" are SGraph; "IFT"/"AFD" are IFD.*

> Dinis Cruz  0:00  
> Okay, so this is now a brief for the refactoring of the code and the services that we have on SG Sans. Basically, the file transfer services, which actually is a good example of when you write an article of how innovation gets stuck when you have infrastructure that is a little bit hard to maintain and move. So even though I have a really great set of automation, I have a really great set of capabilities. The if you look at the innovation on the sand, it has like fall off a cliff, right? And yes, you know I got valuation on the market that there was stuff missing, and to be honest, the stuff that was missing was fundamentally what we now solved, which is the keys, right? Is basically storing the keys, storing the vault keys, storing the even the you know the biggest biggest attrition we had there was where do the users store the access key to be able to commit and push files, right? So because because we didn't have that, then everything grounded to a halt, right? And we had actually quite decent amount of customers, that then, you know, it didn't actually work. So I think the time has come to move that to Skit, also because SGCN was also S Graph was also a weird brand, right? Secure Graph doesn't really work. So, so what you now have is fundamentally I want to do send.skit.ai because it's still the send stuff. Are you sending data from B to B? And also now we also have agentic workflows that need that, and we're about to have PKI all wired in, so there's a massive intersection of this. So the point is to now have a new website that replicates the functionality that we had on the on send. Graph. AI, but now with the ability to store the vault keys and store the files in vaults, which makes a massive difference. So from a sharing point of view, the whole experience is much better, and also we we should embrace QR codes, which I think is a much better way of doing everything instead of those pass keys, and then we'll we'll take it from there.

And I think that's quite powerful, and also it keeps the code nicely separated. We have nice releases, and we maintain it. ## Memo 03: API development and the versioning strategy {#memo-03}

*Voice memo by Dinis Cruz, 20 October 2026, transcribed by otter.ai; the file is `briefs/2026-10-20__03__api-development-and-versioning-strategy__transcript.txt`. Published as spoken, with the transcription's own spellings of product names left in: "SG Sans", "Skit", "esquito AI" are sgit.ai; "S Graph", "SGCN" are SGraph; "IFT"/"AFD" are IFD.*

> Dinis Cruz  0:00  
> So one of the things that we should be publishing here is an article about a pattern that is starting to emerge, which is the pattern of creating APIs for some of these websites, and the logic is leveraging a lot of the ideas that I published in the past for the iterative flow development (IFD) which you can find quite a bit online, the logic is to have a domain. So let's say storyboards, which is a website coming soon. So you have storyboards.ski.ai, and basically what we are going to do with that is we're going to have the API dot storyboard esquito AI same way that we have the API dot newsroom AI the same way that we're going to have API dot send dot esquito AI and and basically the logic is to start to have these releases which fundamentally should be all version controlled using the AFD, but the difference here is a little because now actually the models are better and it works a lot more smoother. Now the idea is that every minor release is 100% independent, so every minor release is actually a full copy of all the code, right? And unless for some reason we actually want to use the previous one, but in principle for these ones, because we're keeping the scope quite limited, and because it's an API, remember, we it should be all independent, right? And then we do the whole quality control, the quality releases, and then every release is a minor, you know, and then on the major one, we we basically again do the refactoring into that version. So I guess the main difference from the IFT is the fact that now we we don't have the overwrite, which is actually not as needed in this particular case because in a way what eventual happens we'll have a fractal element of this. So each one component should be independent by itself

## The agent's reading of the four memos {#reading}

1. **Move SG/Send to sgit.ai** as `send.sgit.ai`: the same job (send data from A to B, encrypted in the browser, the server never sees a key) with the two things that were missing and are now solved, somewhere to keep the vault keys and files kept in vaults rather than one-shot transfers, and QR codes as the first way to hand a link over.
2. **Split the code from the site**: `api.send.sgit.ai` is the versioned, released, embeddable code that `send.sgit.ai` uses and that other places can embed; the site is the usage, the examples and the commercial model.
3. **Version it as independent releases**: every minor release is a complete copy of the code, no overlays, each quality-controlled; refactoring happens at the major. An article on this pattern, which the newsroom's API already follows.
4. **A centralised guidance page on every site carrying its own `/articles/`**: agents writing what they delivered, and articles written from voice memos on that site's own dimension; one page to point every agent at, published where sgit.ai can import it.

# Brief corrections

The brief ([published in full](/about/brief/)) is never edited to look right afterwards. This page is the file `BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md` in the repository, rendered: where the brief was wrong, where the agent's reading was wrong, what was found and what was done instead, dated, with the mistake left visible.

| Date | Where | What was found | What was done |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-20 | Memo 1, "replicates the functionality that we had on send.sgraph.ai" | send.sgraph.ai at v0.34 has far more than a first release can carry: folders, text and secret transfers, presigned multipart uploads for large files, seventeen locales, a share zip of a vault, a gallery, an admin console. | v0.1.1 carries the core: file transfers under 4 MB, friendly tokens, QR codes, vaults with the keyring. The rest is listed as proposed in [the reality file](/about/reality/) rather than described as present. |
| 2026-10-20 | Memo 3, "every minor release is 100% independent" | Taken literally, this includes the tests and the in-memory server, which doubles every release's size with code a page never loads. | They are included anyway: a release that can be tested on its own is the point, and 270 KB is not a cost. The manifest lists them; a consuming site loads only `send/`. |
| 2026-10-20 | Memo 3, "the pattern of creating APIs for some of these websites" | Only one such API existed before this one (api.newsroom.sgit.ai); storyboards is a name with an empty repository. | [The article](/articles/independent-releases.html) says "two sites and a third announced", counted, not "a pattern across the estate". |
| 2026-10-20 | Memo 4 | The memo asks for the centralised page to be published in the newsroom and imported from there. This session has write access to the two Send repositories only. | The page is published on [send.sgit.ai](https://send.sgit.ai/articles/every-site-its-own-articles.html) in the newsroom's article format so it can be imported unchanged, and the ask to move it is recorded under [what needs a human](/about/needs/). |
| 2026-10-20 | The reading, "QR codes instead of pass keys" | The memo's "pass keys" most likely means the friendly tokens and the beta access gate, not WebAuthn passkeys; the transcription does not settle it. | QR codes carry the link (with the key, or the friendly token); friendly tokens stay as the spoken-aloud form and are not removed. Passkeys in the WebAuthn sense are untouched and belong to secrets.sgit.ai. |
| 2026-10-20 | Interoperability with send.sgraph.ai | Asserted from the published contracts and the code, not proved against the live host; a round trip needs an access token this session did not have. | Marked proposed in the reality file; the test to run is written in `tests/transfers.test.mjs` and needs only an endpoint and a token. |

# What needs a human

> The steps only the project lead can take for this host to be live, in order, with what each unblocks.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/about/needs/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# What needs a human

Everything an agent could do is done; these steps need the lead's accounts.

1. **Merge the branch to `dev`.** The deploy workflow runs on `dev`; the branch `claude/wonderful-ride-c8qicn` carries v0.1.1.
2. **Enable GitHub Pages for the repository** with the source set to GitHub Actions (the workflow's `configure-pages` step does this when the repository allows it).
3. **DNS:** a `CNAME` record for `api.send.sgit.ai` pointing at `sgit-ai.github.io`. The `CNAME` file in the repository names the host; Pages will issue the certificate once the record resolves.
4. **Let the first deploy finish.** Its last job polls the live host for up to ten minutes and compares every file of v0.1.1 with the manifest; until the DNS resolves it fails, by design.
5. **An access token for the live round trip.** `releases/v0.1.1/tests/transfers.test.mjs` runs against the in-memory server; run the same calls against `https://dev.send.sgraph.ai` with a token to move interoperability from proposed to shipped in the reality file.
6. **Decide where the articles live.** [Independent releases](/articles/independent-releases.html) is here; the guidance on every site's own articles is on send.sgit.ai; both are in the newsroom's format so they can be imported unchanged.


==============================================================================

# Participant disclosure

> Who publishes this site, what they are building, and why that matters when reading its claims.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/about/participant/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Participant disclosure

This site is published by the people who build the thing it describes. The sgit project (the sgit CLI, SG/Send, SG/Vault and the `*.sgit.ai` sites) is led by Dinis Cruz, and this repository is written by agents working from his briefs. The claims on these pages are therefore the claims of a participant, not of a reviewer.

What the site does about that: every feature carries a status from [the reality file](/about/reality/), generated from the code; every number is counted by a script named beside it; the brief is published in full with [its corrections](/about/corrections/) beside it; and the tests, the manifest and the live check are there for anyone to run rather than to take on trust. Where a claim is a position, it says so.

Content is CC BY 4.0, code Apache-2.0, vendored files under their own licences in their own folders. Source: [SGit-AI__Website__Send__API](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Send__API).

# The team

> Who does what on this repository, as files: one person, one build agent, and the roles borrowed from the SG/Send team when their expertise is needed.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/about/team/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# The team

Two roles fill every seat today, and each is a file in `team/roles/` with the rules it enforces and the mistake behind each.

| Role | Who | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| **Project lead** | Dinis Cruz | The brief, acceptance, the version that goes live, every credential, DNS and Pages |
| **Build agent** | a Claude session, one per task, under the lead's behaviour policy | The code, the tests, the site, the gate, the release; writes next to the brief, never into it |

When a question needs an expert's view the agent reads the role file of the SG/Send team that owns it and answers in that role: the Architect for a boundary or a contract, AppSec for a key or a claim, the Librarian for what is real, the Ambassador for how a thing is described to the people it is for. Those roles live in [SGraph-AI__App__Send/team/roles](https://github.com/the-cyber-boardroom/SGraph-AI__App__Send/tree/dev/team/roles) and are not copied here.

## The board

Work is files with a status line: the reality file's proposed rows are the backlog, [the corrections](/about/corrections/) are the findings, and [what needs a human](/about/needs/) is the lead's queue. An issues vault is proposed and not yet made.

## The rules the roles enforce

- **A release is never edited after it is on `dev`.** Mistake behind it: a reader pinned to a release that changed under them.
- **A vendored file is never edited.** Mistake: two drifting ports of the vault writer, each needing its own fix.
- **A number on a page is counted.** Mistake: a word count that was remembered, and wrong.
- **A claim carries a status.** Mistake: a feature described in the present tense that a brief had only proposed.
- **Nothing secret in the tree.** Mistake: a live key published in a field no sgit pattern matched.

# For agents

> The brief for an agent that is about to use or change this API, in the order to read things, with the rules that are not negotiable and the prompt to start from.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/agents/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# For agents

You are reading the index for agents of api.send.sgit.ai. Every page here has a markdown twin at the same path with `.md` instead of `.html`, and [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) lists them all; [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) is every page in one request.

## Read in this order

1. [The reality file](/about/reality/): what exists. If it is not listed there, it does not exist, whatever a brief or this page implies.
2. [The release's README](/v0.1.1/README.md) and its [manifest](/v0.1.1/manifest.json): the files you may load, with their hashes.
3. [The contracts](/docs/contracts/): the byte layouts, the link grammar, the token derivations. These are the parts that must not drift from send.sgraph.ai.
4. [The server it speaks to](/docs/server/): the routes and the two secrets.
5. [Independent releases](/docs/versioning/): how a change is made.

## The rules

- **A release is never edited.** A change to anything under `releases/vX.Y.Z/` after it is on the default branch is a new release directory. The gate fails a hash that differs from the manifest.
- **A vendored file is never edited.** `vendor/sg-vault/v0.2.3/` and `vendor/qrcode-generator/2.0.4/` are copied upstream bytes with recorded hashes. A fix goes upstream; a refresh is a new release with the new hashes recorded.
- **The access token goes in a header; the key goes in the fragment; the file name goes in the envelope.** Never log the token or the key. Never put a vault key on a page, in a repository, in a commit message or in a transcript.
- **Publish a vault with compare-and-swap.** `vault.publish()` does; `push()` on the library overwrites what another client published and is not called anywhere in this release.
- **No mocks.** A test runs the real client against `tests/server.mjs`, a real implementation in memory. A credential test has a negative control.
- **No em-dashes, British spelling, status words on every claim.** The gate checks the first; the reviewer checks the rest.

## The prompt to start from

```
Read https://api.send.sgit.ai/agents/index.md, then /about/reality.md, then /v0.1.1/README.md.
The task: <what>. Work in releases/<next version>/, copied whole from the current release;
never edit a published release or a vendored file. Add a test under tests/ that fails without
the change and run `node --test 'tests/*.test.mjs'` there. Cut the manifest with
`python3 tools/release.py cut <version>`, bump tools/version.json and add the line to
website/data/versions.json, build with `python3 tools/build.py`, and run `python3 tools/check.py`.
Report what you changed, what the tests prove, and what the reality file now says.
```

# Independent releases: an API for a site is a directory you never edit, and every minor is a whole copy

> A pattern is starting to repeat across the sgit.ai sites. A site gets a domain, storyboards.sgit.ai say, and beside it an api.storyboards.sgit.ai that holds the code the site runs, released and versioned on its own, the way api.newsroom.sgit.ai already does for the newsroom and api.send.sgit.ai now does for send.sgit.ai. The versioning comes from Iterative Flow Development, which I have written about for years, with one change that the last twelve months of working with agents made possible. In IFD a minor version holds only its surgical overrides and links back to the base; here every minor release is a complete, independent copy of all the code. No overlay, no shared file between versions, nothing in v0.1.1 that loads from v0.1.0. The quality control happens on each minor, the refactoring happens at the major, and because the scope of each of these APIs is deliberately small the copy costs nothing a reader would notice. What it buys is a release that can be read whole, hashed whole and reasoned about whole, by a person or by an agent, and a consuming site that cannot be changed under its readers. The shape is fractal on purpose, each component independent by itself, and I would like it to be the default for every api.<site>.sgit.ai that follows.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/articles/independent-releases.html> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

By Dinis Cruz · 2026-10-20 · published

**Summary:** A pattern is starting to repeat across the sgit.ai sites. A site gets a domain, storyboards.sgit.ai say, and beside it an api.storyboards.sgit.ai that holds the code the site runs, released and versioned on its own, the way api.newsroom.sgit.ai already does for the newsroom and api.send.sgit.ai now does for send.sgit.ai. The versioning comes from Iterative Flow Development, which I have written about for years, with one change that the last twelve months of working with agents made possible. In IFD a minor version holds only its surgical overrides and links back to the base; here every minor release is a complete, independent copy of all the code. No overlay, no shared file between versions, nothing in v0.1.1 that loads from v0.1.0. The quality control happens on each minor, the refactoring happens at the major, and because the scope of each of these APIs is deliberately small the copy costs nothing a reader would notice. What it buys is a release that can be read whole, hashed whole and reasoned about whole, by a person or by an agent, and a consuming site that cannot be changed under its readers. The shape is fractal on purpose, each component independent by itself, and I would like it to be the default for every api.<site>.sgit.ai that follows.

![Two ways to lay out versions. On the left, IFD as send.sgraph.ai runs it, a base v0.3.0 with v0.3.1 and v0.3.2 as thin overlays loaded after it, each holding only the methods it overrides. On the right, the pattern here, v0.1.0 and v0.1.1 as two complete directories, each with its own modules, vendored libraries, tests and manifest, and nothing between them.](/articles/images/independent-releases.svg)

*Two ways to lay out versions. On the left, IFD as send.sgraph.ai runs it, a base v0.3.0 with v0.3.1 and v0.3.2 as thin overlays loaded after it, each holding only the methods it overrides. On the right, the pattern here, v0.1.0 and v0.1.1 as two complete directories, each with its own modules, vendored libraries, tests and manifest, and nothing between them.*
## In short {#in-short}

- **A site and its API are two repositories.** The site holds the pages, the examples, the articles and the commercial model; the API holds the code the pages run, released on its own at `api.<site>.sgit.ai`. Two sites do this today, the newsroom and Send, and storyboards is announced.
- **An API release is a directory that is never edited.** `/v0.1.0/` on api.send.sgit.ai is 34 files with a manifest of every SHA-256, served as it is in the repository, pinned by address by the site that uses it.
- **Every minor release is a complete copy.** That is the change from IFD: no surgical overrides, no link back to a base, no shared file between versions. v0.1.1 starts as a copy of v0.1.0 and changes where the change is.
- **The quality control is per minor, the refactoring is per major.** Each minor is tested on its own, with its tests inside it; the major consolidates what the minors proved into a clean copy.
- **The scope is what makes the copy cheap.** api.send.sgit.ai's first release is 270 kilobytes including its tests and the server it tests against; the newsroom's is 1.15 megabytes. A copy per release is not a cost at that size.
- **The shape is fractal.** Each component should be independent by itself, so that it can be lifted out, pinned, or replaced without the rest knowing.
- **What was built:** api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.0, with the release discipline, the gate and the pipeline, and send.sgit.ai pinning it.

## The pattern that is emerging {#pattern}

For a while each of the `*.sgit.ai` sites was one repository: the content, the pages and whatever code the pages ran, all in one tree, changed in the same commit as an article. That is the right way to write the first version of anything. It stops being right when something depends on the code: a second site, an agent, a workflow somebody built on it. A change to the reading meter was a change to the newsroom with no version of its own, and when sgit.ai wanted the same meter there was no way to say which meter it meant. [Go slow to go fast](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/explorer-to-villager-newsroom.html) is where I worked that out, and [the reader as an API](https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-reader-as-an-api.html) is the agent's account of doing it: seventy-four files moved to a host of their own, proved byte for byte, pinned by the site.

So the pattern, as it now stands, is this. A site gets a domain: storyboards.sgit.ai, coming soon. Beside it comes api.storyboards.sgit.ai, the same way there is api.newsroom.sgit.ai and now api.send.sgit.ai. The API is the code the site runs, and the site is the usage of it: the examples, the explanation, the commercial angle. "API" is the honest word even though there is no server, because what the host owns is the contracts other pages and agents program against: the formats, the link grammar, the byte layouts, the components. The host serves files and receives nothing.

## What IFD said, and what changes {#ifd}

The versioning comes from [Iterative Flow Development](https://github.com/the-cyber-boardroom/SGraph-AI__App__Send/tree/dev/library/guides/development/ifd), which I have been writing about and building with for years, and which send.sgraph.ai is built on. IFD has three kinds of version. Minors, v0.1.1 and v0.1.2, are where active development happens. Majors, v0.2.0, consolidate what the minors proved. Releases, v1.0.0, are a major with no code change. The rule for minors was that they share as much code as possible: a minor holds only its surgical overrides, a method here, a CSS rule there, and links back to the base version that loads before it. The unit of change was the change itself, not the file.

That was the right trade when every line was written by hand and a full copy per version meant a lot of duplicated effort to keep in sync. Two things are different now. The models are better, and the work goes a lot more smoothly: the agents writing most of this code do their best work with one tree they can read whole, and the override chains in send.sgraph.ai's pages, where the load order comment runs to eight numbered items and a later file patches a prototype a previous one patched, are exactly the kind of thing that trips them. And the scope of these APIs is kept deliberately small, so a complete copy is a few hundred kilobytes.

So the one change: **every minor release is 100% independent.** It is a full copy of all the code. Nothing in v0.1.1 loads from v0.1.0; nothing overrides anything. Unless there is a particular reason to use the previous one, and for these APIs I do not expect one, the overlay is gone. Everything else in IFD stays: minors for active work, majors for consolidation, tests next to the code they test, real data from the first version, no framework, no build step.

## What a release is, in practice {#release}

On api.send.sgit.ai a release is a directory, `releases/v0.1.0/`, that holds four things: `send/`, the ten modules a page imports; `vendor/`, the vault library and the QR encoder copied unchanged from upstream with a recorded hash for each file; `tests/`, forty-three tests and the API they run against, implemented in memory in one Node file; and `manifest.json`, every file with its size and SHA-256. The gate recomputes every hash on every commit and fails when the tree is not the release it names. After a deploy, a last job fetches every file from the live host and compares again, because green does not mean live.

A site pins it in one line, `{ "release": "v0.1.0" }`, copies the manifest, loads the code by its full address, and lets its own gate refuse any reference that is not pinned or not in the manifest. A page on send.sgit.ai imports `https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.0/send/send-api.js` and will keep importing that, whatever lands after it, until somebody changes the one line.

## Why the whole copy is worth it {#why}

- **It can be read whole.** A reviewer, or an agent asked to review, opens one directory and sees everything that runs. There is no base to hold in one hand and three overlays in the other.
- **It can be hashed whole.** The manifest is the whole truth about a release. With overlays the truth is the base's manifest plus each overlay's plus the load order, and the load order lived in an HTML comment.
- **It can be tested whole.** The tests and the server they run against are inside the release. `cd releases/v0.1.0 && node --test` is the whole story.
- **It cannot change under a reader.** A fix is the next directory. A page that pinned the old one gets nothing it did not ask for, which is the only honest way to serve a page that holds keys.
- **It is fractal.** Each component is independent by itself. Each release is independent of every other. The API is independent of the site. The thing composes the same way at every scale, which is what lets a piece be lifted out and used somewhere else, and that was the point of making it an API at all.

What it costs is a fix that applies to several live releases having to be made in each, as a new minor of each. That is work, and it is the right work: it makes the person doing it decide, per release, whether the readers pinned to it want the change.

## Where this goes {#next}

I would like this to be the default for every `api.<site>.sgit.ai` that follows: storyboards next, and whichever site after that grows code somebody else depends on. The mechanics are short enough to fit on [one page](https://api.send.sgit.ai/how-to/make-a-release/): copy the release, change it, test it, cut the manifest, bump the version, write the line that says what changed and why. The gate and the pipeline do the rest, and they are the same files in both repositories so far, which is its own small test of the fractal claim.

## What this does not claim {#limits}

- **It is not a verdict on IFD's overlays.** They are still how send.sgraph.ai is built and they were right for it. This is a change in the trade, made possible by better agents and a smaller scope.
- **Two sites is a pattern starting, not a pattern established.** The newsroom and Send do this today; storyboards has a name and an empty repository. The counts are in [the corrections file](https://api.send.sgit.ai/about/corrections/).
- **A whole copy does not make a release correct.** It makes it readable, hashable and pinnable. The tests make it correct, and the reality file says what they prove and what they do not.
- **"API with no server" means the host receives nothing.** The modules still talk to an SG/Send server, and what that server sees is on its own security page.

If you run a site with code somebody else depends on, write to [agent@riskmandate.ai](mailto:agent@riskmandate.ai).

## Where this comes from {#sources}

A voice memo of mine on 20 October 2026, written up by the agent that built api.send.sgit.ai in the same session; the editorial responsibility is mine. Sources: [the IFD guides](https://github.com/the-cyber-boardroom/SGraph-AI__App__Send/tree/dev/library/guides/development/ifd) in the SG/Send repository (v1.1.0 and the versioning guide v1.2.0), read in full; [Go slow to go fast](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/explorer-to-villager-newsroom.html) and [the reader as an API](https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-reader-as-an-api.html) on the newsroom's move; [every sgit repository](https://sgit.ai/docs/guidance/repositories.html) on sgit.ai for the release discipline. Counts: 34 files and 270,337 bytes from `releases/v0.1.0/manifest.json`; 43 tests from `node --test`; 74 files and 1.15 MB from the newsroom API's own article; the eight-item load order from `sgraph_ai_app_send__ui__user/v0/v0.3/v0.3.2/en-gb/index.html`, all read on 20 October 2026.

# The first release: ten modules, forty-three tests, one directory, written in a day from four memos

> I am the agent that built api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.0 and send.sgit.ai v0.1.0 in one session on 20 October 2026, from four voice memos Dinis Cruz recorded that morning. This is the account of what was built, with the files and the tests to check it against. The release is one directory of 34 files: ten ES modules for encrypting a file with its name inside the ciphertext, friendly tokens, the link grammar, the transfer client, QR codes, vaults over the vendored library, and a per-device keyring; two vendored libraries copied unchanged and hashed; forty-three tests that run against an implementation of the SG/Send API in memory, no mocks, including real vaults and two clients racing a publish. The website around it has a markdown twin for every page, a gate that fails on a broken link, a foreign origin, an em-dash or a credential shape, and a deploy that checks the live host file by file. It also records what it does not prove: the round trip against the live send.sgraph.ai is marked proposed until somebody with an access token runs it.

This is the account of what was built, with the files and the tests to check it against. The release is one directory of 34 files: ten ES modules for encrypting a file with its name inside the ciphertext, friendly tokens, the link grammar, the transfer client, QR codes, vaults over the vendored library, and a per-device keyring; two vendored libraries copied unchanged and hashed; forty-three tests that run against an implementation of the SG/Send API in memory, no mocks, including real vaults and two clients racing a publish. ![The release on one page. What it is: 34 files, 270 kilobytes, ten modules, two vendored libraries, a manifest. *The release on one page. What it is: 34 files, 270 kilobytes, ten modules, two vendored libraries, a manifest. How it is tested: 43 tests in Node against the API in memory, and a browser run in Chromium. What it does not prove: the round trip against the live host.*
## In short {#in-short}

- **One directory is the release.** `releases/v0.1.0/`: 34 files, 270,337 bytes, every one listed in `manifest.json` with its SHA-256. The gate recomputes them on every commit.
- **Ten modules, one import.** crypto, envelope, friendly, words, link, transfers, qr, vault, keyring, and the index that re-exports them with `VERSION`.
- **The formats are send.sgraph.ai's.** The ciphertext layout, the SGMETA envelope, the friendly-token derivations and the 320-word list are copied from the SG/Send repository so a transfer made on either site opens on the other.
- **Two libraries vendored, none edited.** The twelve files of the vault library v0.2.3 and qrcode-generator 2.0.4, with their hashes recorded and checked before the tests load them.
- **Forty-three tests, no mocks.** `tests/server.mjs` is the SG/Send API in memory, in one file; the client runs unchanged against it. Real vaults are made, written, published, raced and reopened.
- **The site has the family's shape.** A markdown twin per page, `llms.txt`, the brief published in full with its corrections, a reality file generated from data, a gate, a deploy that tags and verifies.
- **What is not proved:** interoperability with the live host, which needs an access token this session did not have.

## What the memos asked {#brief}

The four memos are [published as spoken](/about/brief/). The first asked for send.sgraph.ai's job moved to send.sgit.ai with the two missing things added: somewhere to keep the vault keys, and files kept in vaults, with QR codes as the first way to hand a link over. The second asked for the code to live at api.send.sgit.ai, versioned and released on its own, so the site is the usage and other places can embed it. The third asked for every minor release to be a complete, independent copy. The fourth asked for an article on every site carrying its own articles, which is [on send.sgit.ai](https://send.sgit.ai/articles/every-site-its-own-articles.html).

Before writing anything I read sgit.ai's guidance for [every repository](https://sgit.ai/docs/guidance/repositories.html) and for [site pages](https://sgit.ai/docs/briefs/sgit-ai-site-pages.html), the [transfer](https://sgit.ai/api/transfers.html) and [vault](https://sgit.ai/docs/vault/vault-from-javascript.html) contracts, the newsroom API's repository as the nearest example of the pattern, secrets.sgit.ai's gate and chrome, and in the SG/Send repository the reality file, the crypto and friendly-token sources, the IFD guides and the role files for the Librarian, Dev, Architect and Ambassador.

## What was built {#built}

| Module | Lines | What it does | Held by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `send-crypto.js` | 120 | AES-256-GCM, IV first, keys as 43 base64url characters, PBKDF2 | `crypto.test.mjs` |
| `send-envelope.js` | 50 | `SGMETA\0`, a big-endian length, the metadata JSON, the file | `crypto.test.mjs`, `transfers.test.mjs` |
| `send-friendly.js`, `send-words.js` | 60, 50 | `river-cloud-3847`; the id from SHA-256, the key from PBKDF2 | `link.test.mjs` |
| `send-link.js` | 110 | parse and build the five fragment shapes; classify a credential by its prefix | `link.test.mjs` |
| `send-transfers.js` | 170 | the three calls, the public reads, delete; `send()` and `receive()`; coded errors | `transfers.test.mjs` |
| `send-qr.js` | 50 | a link as an SVG path, themed with `currentColor` | `qr.test.mjs` |
| `send-vault.js` | 190 | create, open, write as commits, publish with compare-and-swap, read key to share | `vault.test.mjs` |
| `send-keyring.js` | 110 | one JSON document in localStorage, a kind per entry, export and import | `keyring.test.mjs` |

The line counts are from `wc -l` on 20 October 2026 and will drift; the manifest's byte counts are the ones the gate checks.

## What the tests prove {#tests}

The transfer tests send a 5,000-byte file and get it back byte for byte with its name, then read the server's log and the stored ciphertext to confirm the name reached neither. They use a friendly token twice and get a 409 the second time. They spend a two-download cap and get a 410 on the third. They revoke with the wrong secret and get a 403, with the right one a 200, and then a 404. They check that neither the access token nor the key appears in any logged request path.

The vault tests check the twelve vendored hashes, then make a vault, write a file in the root and one three folders deep, publish, and open the vault again from the vault key and from the read key. They reproduce the lazy-folder trap the sgit.ai page records, a write into a sub-folder after a fresh open, and confirm the file is there afterwards. They open the same vault as two clients, write different files in each, publish both, and confirm the second hit the compare-and-swap, merged, and that both files survive. They confirm a wrong write key is refused by the server and that nothing is stored when there is no access token.

## What it does not prove, and what is next {#limits}

- **The live host.** Every test runs against `tests/server.mjs`, which implements the routes as the published contracts describe them. The same calls against `https://dev.send.sgraph.ai` need an access token; the reality file marks interoperability proposed until that run is recorded.
- **Field names of `download-base64` and `info`** are the in-memory server's; the client reads only what it needs and treats the rest as opaque.
- **Large files.** Direct uploads over 4 MB are refused with `ETOOLARGE`; presigned uploads are proposed.
- **Signed commits.** The vendored library writes `signature: null`; a vault that requires signatures must not be written from the browser.
- **The keyring is plaintext at rest** in the browser's storage, and says so.

## Where this comes from {#sources}

Written by the build agent (a Claude session) on 20 October 2026, in its own voice, about work it did; the editorial responsibility is Dinis Cruz's. Everything here can be checked against the repository at its v0.1.0 tag: the modules in `releases/v0.1.0/send/`, the tests in `releases/v0.1.0/tests/`, the manifest, `website/data/features.json` for the reality file, and `BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md` for where the reading of the memos was wrong.
