# The modules

> The ten modules of a release, what each exports, and the error codes a caller is expected to act on.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/docs/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# The modules

One import gives every module as a namespace, plus `VERSION` and `RELEASE`:

```js
import * as send from 'https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js'
send.VERSION                       // 'v0.1.1'
send.crypto, send.envelope, send.friendly, send.words, send.link, send.qr, send.vault
send.SendTransfers, send.TransferError, send.Keyring, send.KEYRING_KINDS
```

Each module can also be imported on its own by its path under `send/`.

## crypto, `send/send-crypto.js`

| Export | What it does |
|---|---|
| `generateKey()` | A fresh AES-256-GCM key, extractable |
| `exportKey(key)`, `importKey(str, usages)` | The key as 43 characters of unpadded base64url, and back; `EKEY` if the length is wrong |
| `encryptBytes(key, bytes)` | `IV (12) || ciphertext || tag (16)`, a fresh IV every call |
| `decryptBytes(key, bytes)` | The plaintext, or `EDECRYPT` |
| `deriveKeyPbkdf2(passphrase, salt, iterations = 600000)` | PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 to an AES key |
| `sha256Hex`, `randomBytes`, `bytesToBase64url`, `base64urlToBytes`, `bytesToHex`, `toBytes`, `isKeyString` | Helpers |
| `OVERHEAD` | 28: an encrypted payload is exactly this much larger than its plaintext |

## envelope, `send/send-envelope.js`

`wrap(meta, bytes)` puts `{ filename, ... }` in front of the file under the `SGMETA\0` magic; `unwrap(bytes)` returns `{ meta, bytes, enveloped }`. Bytes without an envelope come back whole with an empty meta, so an older transfer still opens. [The byte layout](/docs/contracts/#envelope).

## friendly, `send/send-friendly.js`

`newFriendlyToken()` makes `word-word-1234` from the 320-word list in `send-words.js`; `isFriendlyToken(s)`; `deriveTransferId(token)` is the first 12 hex of SHA-256; `deriveKey(token)` is PBKDF2 with salt `sgraph-send-v1`. `COMBINATIONS` is 1,024,000,000.

## link, `send/send-link.js`

| Export | What it does |
|---|---|
| `parseFragment(urlOrHash)` | `{ kind }` of `transfer` (with `transferId`, `key` or null), `friendly` (`token`), `vault-key` or `read-key` (`vaultId`, `secret`, `declared`), `empty`, `unknown`. Never throws |
| `transferLink`, `friendlyLink`, `vaultLink` | Build a link on an open page: `{ openUrl, ... }` |
| `classifyCredential(s)` | `vault`, `read-public`, `read-private` or `unknown`, by the declared prefix |
| `parseVaultCredential(s)` | `{ kind: 'vault' or 'read', secret, vaultId, declared }`, prefix first, shape second |
| `publicReadKey(hex, vaultId)`, `privateVaultKey(passphrase, vaultId)` | The prefixed forms |

## transfers, `send/send-transfers.js`

`new SendTransfers({ endpoint, accessToken })`. The three calls `create`, `upload`, `complete`; the public `info`, `download`, `downloadBase64`; `remove(id, deleteSecret)`; `health()`. The whole job: `send({ bytes, filename, friendlyToken, maxDownloads, expiresAt, revocable, onProgress })` returns `{ transferId, keyString, friendlyToken, encryptedBytes, deleteSecret }`; `receive({ transferId, keyString } or { friendlyToken })` returns `{ filename, meta, bytes }`.

Errors are `TransferError` with a `code`:

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `EAUTH` | 401: no access token, or a wrong one |
| `EFORBIDDEN` | 403: for example a wrong delete secret |
| `ENOTFOUND` | 404: never existed, or deleted. An end state, not a retry |
| `EGONE` | 410: expired or exhausted. Also an end state |
| `ETOOLARGE` | A direct upload over 4 MB, refused before any request; or 413 from the server |
| `EDECRYPT`, `EKEY` | Wrong key; no key where one was needed |
| `ENETWORK` | The host could not be reached |
| `EEDGE` | The edge answered with an HTML page; the status cannot be trusted |

## qr, `send/send-qr.js`

`toSvg(text, { ecc, margin, size, dark, light, title })` returns an SVG string with one path; `toDataUrl(text)` the same for an `<img>`; `modules(text)` the grid; `fits(text, ecc)`. Colours default to `currentColor` on a transparent background, so a code takes the page's theme.

## vault, `send/send-vault.js`

`await ready()` loads the vendored library from this release; `client({ endpoint, accessToken })`; `createVault(sg, { name })` returns `{ vault, vaultId, vaultKey, readKey }`; `openVault(sg, vaultKey)` (a read key opens read-only); `openReadOnly(sg, readKey)`; `writeFile`, `writeFiles` (one commit for many files), `readFile`, `readText`, `listFolder`, `listAll`, `history`; `publish(vault)` with compare-and-swap and a merge on `ECAS`; `readKeyOf(vault)`; `randomPassphrase()`; `cloneBranch()`. Every folder is loaded before a write into it, which is the trap the sgit.ai page records.

## keyring, `send/send-keyring.js`

`new Keyring({ storage })`, `KINDS` (`sgit-vault-key`, `sgit-read-key`, `send-transfer`, `send-access-token`), `list({ kind })`, `get`, `add({ kind, label, value, ...meta })`, `update`, `remove`, `clear`, `exportJson()`, `importJson(text)`. One JSON document under `send.sgit.ai.keyring.v1` in the page's localStorage, plaintext at rest, per device.

## words, `send/send-words.js`

`WORDS`, frozen, 320 entries; `WORD_COUNT`; `COMBINATIONS`. The list send.sgraph.ai has used since v0.2.6, so a token made by either site opens on the other.


==============================================================================

# Contracts, the formats that must not drift

> The byte layouts and string grammars this release shares with send.sgraph.ai and with sgit, each with where it came from and the test that holds it.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/docs/contracts/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Contracts: links, envelope, tokens, keys

These are the parts that have to match on both ends: a sender on one site, a reader on another, a CLI on a laptop. Each one names its source and the test that holds it. A change to any of them is a new major version of this API and a conversation with the owners of the other end.

## The ciphertext {#ciphertext}

```
IV                 12 bytes    random, fresh per encryption, prepended
ciphertext + tag   rest        AES-256-GCM; GCM appends its own 16-byte tag
```

Exactly what `crypto.subtle.encrypt` returns with the IV in front, so a payload is 28 bytes larger than its plaintext. The key is 32 random bytes, shared as unpadded base64url, 43 characters. Source: send.sgraph.ai since v0.1.1, documented at [sgit.ai/api/transfers](https://sgit.ai/api/transfers.html). Held by `tests/crypto.test.mjs`.

## The envelope {#envelope}

```
"SGMETA\0"       7 bytes    53 47 4D 45 54 41 00
meta_len         4 bytes    uint32, big-endian
metadata JSON    meta_len   {"filename": "..."} UTF-8
file bytes       rest
```

Wrapped before encrypting, so the name is inside the ciphertext. Getting the order wrong produces a corrupt download with no name. Held by `tests/crypto.test.mjs` (magic, length, round trip) and `tests/transfers.test.mjs` (the name appears in no request and not in the stored bytes).

## Friendly tokens {#friendly}

| | |
|---|---|
| Shape | `word-word-DDDD`, two words from the 320-word list and four digits, `/^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-\d{4}$/` |
| Transfer id | the first 12 hex characters of `SHA-256(token)` |
| Key | `PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(token, salt "sgraph-send-v1", 600000)`, 256 bits |
| Create | the client sends `transfer_id` in the create body; the server refuses an id that exists |

Source: send.sgraph.ai `friendly-crypto.js` and `V026_WORDS`. Held by `tests/link.test.mjs` (the id computed independently) and `tests/transfers.test.mjs` (a token used twice is refused).

## Links {#links}

The fragment, after `#`, split on the first `/`, truncated at `|`:

| Fragment | Means |
|---|---|
| `<transfer_id>/<key>` | a transfer and its 43-character key |
| `<transfer_id>` | link only; the key travels by another channel |
| `<word-word-1234>` | a friendly token |
| `<prefix><secret>:<vault_id>` | a vault credential; the prefix declares which |

`transfer_id` is `/^[a-z0-9]{8,32}$/i`; `vault_id` is `/^[a-z0-9]{4,24}$/`. Source: send.sgraph.ai's download page and sgit.ai's credentials page. Held by `tests/link.test.mjs`.

## Vault credentials {#credentials}

| Prefix | Declares | May be published |
|---|---|---|
| `sgit_private_vault_` | a vault key, read and write | never |
| `sgit_private_read_` | a read key kept private | no; re-derive under the public prefix first |
| `sgit_public_read_` | a read key, deliberately published | yes |
| `sgit_vk1_`, `sgit_rk1_` | legacy forms, accepted, never emitted | as above |

Classification is by declaration first and shape second: a bare `<64 hex>:<id>` reads as a read key, anything else before the colon is a passphrase, which is write access. Source: [sgit.ai/docs/credentials](https://sgit.ai/docs/credentials.html) and the vendored `SGVaultCrypto.classifyKey`. Held by `tests/link.test.mjs`.

## The vault objects {#vault}

The vendored library owns this contract and this release does not restate it: read key and write key derived by PBKDF2 from the passphrase and the vault id, `obj-cas-imm-` content-addressed objects, `ref-pid-muw-` refs, one `POST /batch` per commit, compare-and-swap on publish. [Creating and writing a vault from JavaScript](https://sgit.ai/docs/vault/vault-from-javascript.html) is the reference; `tests/vault.test.mjs` proves create, write, publish, race and reopen against the in-memory server, and the hashes of the twelve files before any of it.

## The keyring document {#keyring}

```json
{ "version": 1, "entries": [ { "id", "kind", "label", "value", "created", ...meta } ] }
```

`kind` is one of `sgit-vault-key`, `sgit-read-key`, `send-transfer`, `send-access-token`. The document is this release's own format; `exportJson()` adds `exported` and `origin`. Held by `tests/keyring.test.mjs`.


==============================================================================

# Hosting and pinning

> How a release is served, what a consuming site pins and checks, the CORS the host sends, and the subresource integrity question.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/docs/hosting/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Hosting and pinning

## How a release is served

`dev` is the release branch. A push runs the gate, tags the version, assembles the Pages tree (`www/` at the root and every `releases/vX.Y.Z/` directory beside it as `/vX.Y.Z/`) and deploys it; a last job then fetches every file of the current release from the live host and compares its hash with the manifest. `/releases.json` lists every release with its date, file count and size.

GitHub Pages sends `access-control-allow-origin: *`, which is what lets a module on this host be imported by a page on another, and it has no way to receive a request.

## What a site pins

```json
{ "host": "https://api.send.sgit.ai", "release": "v0.1.1" }
```

One file, one line. The site copies the release's `manifest.json` beside it, and its gate fails the build on a reference to this host that is not pinned to that release or not a path in the manifest. send.sgit.ai does this in `admin/build/api.json` and its `tools/check.py`.

## Subresource integrity

A `<script type="module">` with an `integrity` attribute works for the entry module but not for the modules it imports, so this host does not promise SRI for the whole graph. What it promises instead: a release directory is never edited, the manifest carries every hash, and the live check runs after every deploy. A site that must not change under its readers (one holding keys) copies the release into its own origin at a known commit, as [the vault-from-JavaScript page](https://sgit.ai/docs/vault/vault-from-javascript.html) asks, and the gate's origin check lets that through because the files are then its own.

## Caching

Release files are immutable by construction, so a CDN may cache them for as long as it likes. `releases.json` and the website's pages change on every version; keep a short freshness window on those.


==============================================================================

# The server it speaks to

> The routes this release calls on the SG/Send API, the two secrets, what the in-memory server in tests/server.mjs implements, and the field names it has not verified against production.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/docs/server/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# The server it speaks to

The modules talk HTTP to an SG/Send API host. The hosted one is `https://send.sgraph.ai` (and `https://dev.send.sgraph.ai` for development); anyone can [run their own](https://sgit.ai/deploy/); and `tests/server.mjs` in every release is the same routes in memory, in one Node process, for the tests and for a page on a laptop.

## Transfers

| Call | Auth | What the client sends and expects |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/transfers/create` | token | `{ file_size_bytes, content_type_hint, max_downloads, auto_delete, expires_at, transfer_id?, delete_auth_hash? }` → `{ transfer_id }`. `expires_at` is milliseconds; 0 is never. `max_downloads` 0 is unlimited |
| `POST /api/transfers/upload/{id}` | token | raw bytes, `application/octet-stream` |
| `POST /api/transfers/complete/{id}` | token | nothing is downloadable before this |
| `GET /api/transfers/info/{id}` | none | metadata: status, size, content type hint, download count |
| `GET /api/transfers/download/{id}` | none | the bytes; 410 once expired or exhausted; 404 when it never existed or was deleted |
| `GET /api/transfers/download-base64/{id}` | none | the same bytes in JSON |
| `DELETE /api/transfers/delete/{id}` | token + `x-sgraph-transfer-delete-auth` | only if a `delete_auth_hash` was set at create |
| `GET /api/info/health`, `GET /api/info/version` | none | the server's own health and version. **Not** `/api/health`: measured a 404 there on 20 October 2026, which v0.1.0 got wrong |

## Vaults

`GET /api/vault/read/{vault}/{file}` (public), `PUT /api/vault/write/{vault}/{file}` and `POST /api/vault/batch/{vault}` (token and `x-sgraph-vault-write-key`), `DELETE /api/vault/delete/...`, `GET /api/vault/presigned/read-url/...` for files over 4 MB. The vendored library makes these calls; this release never does directly. [API: vault objects](https://sgit.ai/api/vault-objects.html).

## The two secrets

The **access token** is presented as `x-sgraph-access-token`. The API also accepts `?access_token=` as a query fallback; this release never uses it, because query strings land in logs. The **decryption key** is never presented to the server at all.

## What the in-memory server implements

Everything in the two tables, plus `GET /api/health` and `GET /api/presigned/capabilities` (reporting no presigned support), with CORS as measured on the real host: any origin, the sgraph headers allowed, `X-API-Key` refused on preflight. It records methods, paths and statuses in a log the tests read, and never a key or a token.

## Measured against the hosted service, 20 October 2026

After the first deploy, from this repository: `send.sgraph.ai` answers a preflight from `https://send.sgit.ai` with `access-control-allow-origin: *` and allows every header this release sends (`x-sgraph-access-token`, `x-sgraph-vault-write-key`, `x-sgraph-vault-enum-key`, `x-sgraph-transfer-delete-auth`); `GET /api/transfers/info/<unknown>` is a 404 in under a second; `/api/health` is a 404 and the health route is `/api/info/health`, which is the v0.1.1 fix.

## What is not verified against production

Stated here rather than guessed at, per [the reality file](/about/reality/):

- The JSON field names of `download-base64` (`content_base64`, `size`) are this server's; the production names were not checked.
- `info`'s field set is this server's; the client reads `content_type_hint`, `download_count` and `status` and treats the rest as opaque.
- A client-chosen `transfer_id` on create is documented in the SG/Send code (`Schema__Transfer__Create.transfer_id`) and used by send.sgraph.ai's friendly tokens; the 409 on a taken id is this server's choice of status.
- The edge in front of `send.sgraph.ai` has rewritten some 403s to an HTML 404 page; the client reports `EEDGE` when a body starts with `<` and says the status cannot be trusted.


==============================================================================

# Versioning, independent releases

> Every minor release is a complete copy of the code with no overlays and no shared files; majors are where the refactoring happens. The rules, the reasons, and how this differs from the IFD that came before it.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/docs/versioning/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Versioning: independent releases

## The rule

Every release under `releases/` is a complete, independent copy of the code. `v0.1.1` starts as a copy of `v0.1.1`, changed where the change is; nothing in it imports from `v0.1.1`, overrides a method of `v0.1.1`, or loads a stylesheet of `v0.1.1`. A page that pins `v0.1.1` keeps running `v0.1.1` whatever lands after it.

| Kind | Example | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Minor** | v0.1.1, v0.1.2 | Copy the current release whole, make the change, add the test that fails without it, cut the manifest. Quality control on each |
| **Major** | v0.2.0 | Consolidate: refactor what the minors proved into a clean copy, retire what did not survive, keep the contracts |
| **Release** | v1.0.0 | The previous major with no code change: version and documentation only |

## Why no overlays this time

The [IFD methodology](https://github.com/the-cyber-boardroom/SGraph-AI__App__Send/tree/dev/library/guides/development/ifd) that send.sgraph.ai is built with shares code between minor versions: a minor holds only its surgical overrides and links back to the base, so `v0.3.2` is `v0.3.0` plus two patch files loaded after it. That was the right trade when every line was written by hand and a full copy per version was a cost. Two things changed. The code here is small and its scope is deliberately narrow, so a copy is a few hundred kilobytes. And the agents that now write most of it work better with one tree they can read whole than with a base and three layers of overrides to compose in their heads; the override chains in send.sgraph.ai's `index.html` (load order comments eight items long) are the evidence. So the overlay goes, and what stays from IFD is everything else: minors for active development, majors for consolidation, tests co-located with what they test, real data from the first version, zero external dependencies.

## What it costs, and what it buys

- **Costs:** disk, trivially; and a fix that applies to several live releases has to be made in each, as a new minor of each, which is the point: a reader pinned to an old release gets nothing they did not ask for.
- **Buys:** a release that can be read, reviewed, hashed and reasoned about on its own; a manifest that is the whole truth; a consuming site that cannot be changed under its readers; and a fractal shape, where each component is independent by itself and can be lifted out, which is where this is going.

## The mechanics

1. `cp -r releases/v0.1.1 releases/v0.1.1`, then make the change in `v0.1.1` only.
2. `VERSION = 'v0.1.1'` in `send/send-api.js`; the gate checks it matches the directory.
3. A test in `tests/` that fails without the change; `node --test 'tests/*.test.mjs'` green.
4. `python3 tools/release.py cut v0.1.1` writes the manifest; `tools/version.json` says `release: v0.1.1`.
5. A line in `website/data/versions.json` that says what changed and why, in words a reader can act on.
6. `python3 tools/build.py && python3 tools/check.py`, commit, push. `dev` deploys, tags, and checks the live host.

[How to make a release](/how-to/make-a-release/) is the same list as a checklist. The article that argues this out is [Independent releases](/articles/independent-releases.html).


==============================================================================

# For developers

> How to take a release into a site, what to pin, what the gate should check, what runs where, and how to run the tests and the server in memory.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/for-developers/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# For developers

## Take a release

1. Name the release in one file of your site, for example `build/api.json`: `{ "host": "https://api.send.sgit.ai", "release": "v0.1.1" }`.
2. Copy `https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/manifest.json` next to it, so your build knows the hash of every file it may load.
3. Load the code by its full address, `https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js`, in a `<script type="module">` or an import map.
4. Add a check to your gate: every reference to this host is pinned to the release you named and is a path in the manifest. send.sgit.ai's gate does exactly this.

A script loaded from another host still runs on your page's origin, so the keyring, the clone branch and everything the modules store stay in your site's storage. This host has no way to receive anything.

## What runs where

| Module | Browser | Node 20+ | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| crypto, envelope, friendly, words, link, keyring | yes | yes | `globalThis.crypto` (a secure context in a browser) |
| transfers | yes | yes | `fetch`; an access token for writes |
| qr | yes | yes | nothing |
| vault | yes | yes, after loading the twelve library files into the realm (`tests/_lib.mjs` shows how) | an access token for creating and writing |

## Run the tests

```
cd releases/v0.1.1
node --test 'tests/*.test.mjs'
```

43 tests, about four seconds, no network: `tests/server.mjs` starts the API in memory on a random port and the client code runs unchanged against it. [How to run the tests](/how-to/run-the-tests/) has the rest, including the browser run.

## Run the server for local development

```
node releases/v0.1.1/tests/server.mjs 8787 local-dev-token
```

Point a page at `http://localhost:8787` with the access token `local-dev-token` and everything works without an account: transfers, vaults, download caps, expiry, revocation. It forgets everything when it stops. [The server it speaks to](/docs/server/) lists the routes.

## Make a change

A change to a served file is a new release: copy `releases/v0.1.1/` to `releases/v0.1.1/`, make the change there with a test that fails without it, cut the manifest, bump `tools/version.json`, and let the gate and the pipeline do the rest. [How to make a release](/how-to/make-a-release/) is the checklist; [independent releases](/docs/versioning/) is why it works this way.


==============================================================================

# For evaluators

> The trust boundaries, what leaves the browser and what never does, the supply chain of this release and how to verify the live host yourself.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/for-evaluators/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# For evaluators

## What leaves the browser, and what never does

| Leaves the browser | Never leaves |
|---|---|
| The ciphertext (IV, encrypted bytes, GCM tag) | The plaintext |
| The plaintext length, as display metadata | The file name: it is inside the ciphertext, in the SGMETA envelope |
| A `content_type_hint` the sender chooses; keep it generic | The decryption key: it is in the link's fragment, which browsers do not send |
| The access token, in a request header, to the API host only | The vault key, the read key, the keyring: this host receives nothing at all |
| For a vault: encrypted objects, refs and the write key's hex in a header, which the server stores only as a hash | The passphrase the vault key is made of |

The API host, `api.send.sgit.ai`, is GitHub Pages: it serves files and has no way to receive a request body. The server the modules talk to is `send.sgraph.ai` or whichever endpoint the page configures, and what that server can and cannot see is written up at [sgit.ai's security page](https://sgit.ai/security/).

## Two secrets that must not be confused

The **access token** says who may upload. The **decryption key** says who may read. They are unrelated values with unrelated jobs, and the failure that matters is silent: an access token in a URL lands in proxy logs and browser history; a key in a request reaches a server that should never have it. `send-transfers.js` puts the token in `x-sgraph-access-token` and nowhere else, and the tests assert that neither value appears in any logged request path.

## The supply chain of a release

- **Twelve vault library files** from SGraph-AI__App__Send at a named commit, copied unchanged, with a SHA-256 per file in `VENDOR.md`. The tests recompute every hash before loading a single one.
- **One QR encoder**, qrcode-generator 2.0.4, with its hash in its README.
- **Nothing else.** No framework, no bundler, no build step for the served code, nothing fetched at run time from any other origin. The gate fails a page that loads a script or a style from another host.
- **A manifest** of every file in the release with its size and SHA-256, recomputed by the gate on every commit and by the live check after every deploy.

## Verify the live host yourself

```
curl -s https://api.send.sgit.ai/releases.json | python3 -m json.tool
curl -s https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/manifest.json > manifest.json
python3 - <<'PY'
import hashlib, json, urllib.request
m = json.load(open('manifest.json'))
for f, e in m['entries'].items():
    b = urllib.request.urlopen(f"https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/{f}").read()
    print('ok ' if hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest() == e['sha256'] else 'BAD', f)
PY
```

That is the same check `tools/live_check.py` runs at the end of every deploy. Until the DNS for this host is in place ([what needs a human](/about/needs/)), run it against the repository instead: `python3 tools/release.py check`.

## What this does not prove

- **Interoperability with the live send.sgraph.ai** is asserted from the published contracts and the in-memory server, not from a run against the production host. [The reality file](/about/reality/) marks it proposed until a round trip is recorded.
- **The keyring is plaintext at rest** in the browser's storage, and the page that uses it says so. The passkey-unlocked design at [secrets.sgit.ai](https://secrets.sgit.ai) is the stronger home.
- **A friendly token is guessable offline** by anyone holding the ciphertext: 1,024,000,000 possibilities and a 600,000-round derivation per guess. It is for links that expire.


==============================================================================

# How to make a release

> The checklist, from copying the current release to checking the live host, with the commands.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/how-to/make-a-release/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# How to make a release

```
cp -r releases/v0.1.1 releases/v0.1.1          # 1. a complete copy; change only v0.1.1
# 2. make the change, and a test under releases/v0.1.1/tests/ that fails without it
sed -i "s/VERSION = 'v0.1.1'/VERSION = 'v0.1.1'/" releases/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js
(cd releases/v0.1.1 && node --test 'tests/*.test.mjs')
python3 tools/release.py cut v0.1.1            # 3. the manifest
# 4. tools/version.json: version v0.1.1, release v0.1.1, today's date
# 5. website/data/versions.json: a new first entry, one sentence that says what changed and why
python3 tools/build.py && python3 tools/check.py
git add -A && git commit -m "api v0.1.1 : what changed" && git push
```

A change that touches only the website, the tests or the tooling bumps `version` and leaves `release` where it is. The deploy tags the version, publishes, and then runs `tools/live_check.py`; a clean push is not a release until that last job is green.

What the gate will refuse: a release directory whose files differ from its manifest, a vendored file that differs from its recorded hash, a page without a twin, a broken link, a script from another origin, an em-dash, a credential shape, a version that is not the newest in `versions.json`.

# How to run the tests

> The Node tests against the in-memory server, the browser smoke test in Chromium, and the gate; what each proves.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/how-to/run-the-tests/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# How to run the tests

## In Node, against the server in memory

```
cd releases/v0.1.1
node --test 'tests/*.test.mjs'
```

43 tests in about four seconds. `tests/server.mjs` starts on a random port; every test runs the real client against it. `tests/vault.test.mjs` first checks the hash of each of the twelve vendored files against `VENDOR.md`, then loads them into the realm the way a page does, then makes real vaults: create, nested writes after a fresh open, two clients racing a publish, history, a wrong write key refused.

## In a browser

```
node tests/test_browser.mjs
```

Starts the in-memory server and a static server for the release, opens `tests/browser.html` in Chromium with Playwright, and checks that the same modules load as ES modules on a page, encrypt and decrypt, draw a QR code, send and receive a transfer, and create and read back a vault. The pre-installed Chromium is used when Playwright has none of its own.

## The gate

```
python3 tools/check.py
```

What CI runs on every commit. [The modules](/docs/) lists the error codes the tests exercise; [for evaluators](/for-evaluators/) says what the tests do not prove.

# Releases

A release is a directory under `/vX.Y.Z/` on this host, served exactly as it is in the repository, with a `manifest.json` of every file's size and SHA-256. The current one is named in [`/releases.json`](/releases.json). A change to the code is the next directory, never an edit of this one; [independent releases](/docs/versioning/) is the rule and the reason.

| Release | Date | Files | Bytes | Manifest | README |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **v0.1.1** | 2026-10-20 | 36 | 276,069 | [manifest.json](/v0.1.1/manifest.json) | [README](/v0.1.1/README.md) |
| **v0.1.0** | 2026-10-20 | 36 | 274,733 | [manifest.json](/v0.1.0/manifest.json) | [README](/v0.1.0/README.md) |

The website around the releases has versions of its own, one per change that lands on `dev`; [the version history](/versions/) has a line for each.

# Quick start, send a file from a page

> Twelve lines to encrypt a file in the browser, upload it as a transfer, and hand over a link and a QR code; and the two lines that open it.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/start/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Quick start: send a file from a page

Three things to have in their places before the first line of code. **The access token** authorises you to upload; it travels in a request header and never in a URL. **The key** lets anyone read; it travels in the link's fragment, after `#`, which a browser never sends to a server. **The file name** travels inside the ciphertext, so the server never sees it. Confuse the first two and nothing throws, which is why this page says it first.

## 1. Pin the release and import it

```html
<script type="module">
  import * as send from 'https://api.send.sgit.ai/v0.1.1/send/send-api.js'
</script>
```

The address names the release. A later release is a different directory; this one does not change. [Hosting and pinning](/docs/hosting/) says how a site's build can check that.

## 2. Send

```js
const api = new send.SendTransfers({ endpoint: 'https://send.sgraph.ai', accessToken: token })   // the token: a header, never a URL
const file = input.files[0]
const r = await api.send({
  bytes:       new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer()),
  filename:    file.name,                 // goes inside the envelope, encrypted
  maxDownloads: 0,                        // 0 is unlimited
  expiresAt:   Date.now() + 7 * 86400e3,  // milliseconds since the epoch; 0 is never
  onProgress:  step => console.log(step)  // wrap, encrypt, create, upload, complete
})
const url = send.link.transferLink({ openUrl: 'https://send.sgit.ai/open/', transferId: r.transferId, key: r.keyString })
qrBox.innerHTML = send.qr.toSvg(url, { title: 'scan to open' })
```

`r.keyString` is the 43-character key. Put it in the link, or hand the link without it (`key: null`) and send the key by a second channel. Never log it: anyone holding it reads the file.

## 3. Open

```js
const parsed = send.link.parseFragment(location.hash)     // { kind: 'transfer', transferId, key } or 'friendly', 'vault-key', 'read-key'
const got = await new send.SendTransfers({ endpoint: 'https://send.sgraph.ai' })
  .receive({ transferId: parsed.transferId, keyString: parsed.key })
saveAs(got.bytes, got.filename)                           // byte for byte what was sent, and the name that never left the browser
```

Opening needs no token: `info` and `download` are public by design, and the key is the gate.

## A friendly token instead of a key

```js
const token = send.friendly.newFriendlyToken()            // "river-cloud-3847"
await api.send({ bytes, filename, friendlyToken: token })
const url = send.link.friendlyLink({ openUrl: 'https://send.sgit.ai/open/', token })
```

One string that can be read out over the phone, and that a QR code carries in a smaller square. Both the transfer id and the key derive from it, so the server never maps a token to anything. There are 1,024,000,000 possible tokens, guessable offline by anyone who has the ciphertext: a friendly token suits a link that expires; a random key suits one that must not be guessed.

## Into a vault instead of a transfer

```js
await send.vault.ready()                                                // loads the vendored library from this release
const sg = send.vault.client({ endpoint: 'https://send.sgraph.ai', accessToken: token })
const { vault, vaultKey, readKey } = await send.vault.createVault(sg, { name: 'Project files' })
await send.vault.writeFiles(vault, [{ folder: '/', name: file.name, data: bytes }])
await send.vault.publish(vault)                                        // compare-and-swap, never push()
keyring.add({ kind: send.KEYRING_KINDS.VAULT_KEY, label: 'Project files', value: vaultKey })   // read and write: stays on this device
shareUrl = send.link.vaultLink({ openUrl: 'https://send.sgit.ai/open/', credential: readKey })  // read only: this one may be shared
```

A vault is versioned, browsable, updatable, and clonable with `sgit clone <read key>`. [The modules](/docs/) have the full surface; [the contracts](/docs/contracts/) have the byte layouts.


==============================================================================

# Version history

> One line per version, newest first, saying what changed and why. Every change that lands on dev is a version; the deploy tags it.

*Source: <https://api.send.sgit.ai/versions/> · api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.1 · this file is generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Every page on this site has a `.md` twin; internal links below point at pages, swap `.html` for `.md` to read the twin.*

---

# Version history

Every change that lands on `dev` is a version, in `tools/version.json`, tagged by the deploy and shown in the header of every page. The `release` column is the cut of the code a site pins; it moves only when a served file changes.

| Version | Date | Kind | What changed, and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **v0.1.1** | 2026-10-20 | fix | **the health check asks the route the hosted service serves.** Measured against send.sgraph.ai after the first deploy: /api/health is a 404 there and the health route is /api/info/health, so Settings on send.sgit.ai reported the hosted server as not answering. v0.1.1 is a whole copy of v0.1.0 with health() on /api/info/health, a new version() on /api/info/version, the in-memory server serving the same two routes and answering 404 on /api/health as production does, and a test that holds all of that. The CORS check the same run made is recorded on the server page: the hosted service allows any origin and every header this release sends. |
| **v0.1.0** | 2026-10-20 | release | **the first release: the modules send.sgit.ai runs, as one independent directory, with its tests and the server in memory.** From the four voice memos of 20 October 2026 (the brief, published in full). The modules: AES-256-GCM crypto with the SGMETA envelope, friendly tokens with the derivations send.sgraph.ai uses, the link grammar, the transfer client with send() and receive(), QR codes as SVG, the vault layer over the vendored library (publish with compare-and-swap, never push()), and the per-device keyring. 43 tests run in Node against the in-memory server; a browser smoke test runs the same modules in Chromium. The website, the gate and the release tooling come with it. |
